faq.q: What are product color variation photos?
faq.a: A square set of one product in the shades you actually sell, shown in one shared scene so shoppers compare the finish. Each shade starts from a photo of that color.

faq.q: How do I make product color variations?
faq.a: Upload one photo per real shade, describe the setting once, and download a square for each. The same photos can also start a clip with a script and a voice.

faq.q: Why use this instead of a new shoot for every color?
faq.a: The scene is applied to photos you already have, so you skip a styled reshoot. A generated color cannot stand in for a shade you never photographed.

faq.q: Who is a color set for?
faq.a: Shops that sell more than one finish, including sneakers, apparel, mugs, cases and yarn, on Shopify or Amazon.

faq.q: Can a beginner make the set?
faq.a: Yes. Upload the shade photos and use the same description on each. No editing background is required. Compare every file with the physical swatch before you publish.

faq.q: Which products fit a color set?
faq.a: Any product whose dye, glaze, fabric or finish changes, as long as you photograph the real shade. One scene can cover several products when each source photo is real.

faq.q: Can I upload my own photos?
faq.a: Yes. Upload your own shade photos. A file is not a guaranteed color match, so keep the real swatch nearby and compare before you publish.

faq.q: Which platforms can I use the files on?
faq.a: Listing galleries on Amazon and Shopify, plus TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and YouTube when you also make a clip from the same photos.
No. There is no free plan. Each product photo costs 24 credits, the total is shown first, and a failed job returns those credits. Plans start at $24.50 a month.

faq.q: Can I use the set commercially?
faq.a: Yes. Add each image to the matching option in your own listing or ads. The download has no watermark.

faq.q: Why start from a shared scene?
faq.a: The shared scene keeps the view, light and background steady, so shoppers compare color instead of a changing setup. You still check every hue against the item.

faq.q: Can a voice, a presenter or a product link be part of this?
faq.a: Yes. Paste the product page link, or send a photo through the API, to draft a script, a presenter and a voice in another language. The shade squares still come from real photos.
